Delivered The Following:

Maca No. 885 Of 2015
 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P (MV) No.695 of 2006 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thrissur, seeking enhancement of compensation.
The respondents herein were the respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the claimant, on 11.01.2006, while he was travelling in an auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KL-08- 4302 through Thrissur-Palakkad public road, a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AE-9457 driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the auto-rickshaw and thereby he sustained serious injuries.
He approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 4,50,000/-.
3. The respondents 1 and 2 being the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle, remained ex-parte before the tribunal.
The 3rd respondent insurer filed a written statement admitting the policy, but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed and denying liability.
Before the tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A15 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 65,300/- with 7.5% interest from the date of petition till realization, as 2026:KER:10124 MACA NO. 885 OF 2015 compensation under different heads against the 3 rd respondent being the insurer.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant and the learned standing counsel for the respondent insurance company.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads:-
Notional income :-

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 4,000/- was claimed as the income of the injured, who was a heavy duty driver, the tribunal had taken only an amount of 2,500/-.

The learned counsel submitted that even going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.Ltd [2011 (13) SCC 236], the income of a Coolie, for an accident that occurred in the year 2006, is fixed as 5,500/- and seeks enhancement of the income fixed.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.Ltd [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to award a just and reasonable compensation, following the judgment in Ramachandrappa (supra), I find it appropriate to fix the income at 5,500/-.
2026:KER:10124 MACA NO. 885 OF 2015 Loss of earnings :
- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that for awarding compensation under the head loss of earnings, the tribunal has taken only a period of three months.

The claimant has Manoj.K.M vs R.Babu on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73417763/
2 sustained head injury and multiple fractures in the facial bones.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained, I find that a period of six months can be taken for awarding compensation under the afore head.
Accordingly, the total compensation payable under the head loss of earnings is re-
calculated to 33,000/- (5500 x 6).
The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 7,500/- under the afore head.

Thus,
there will be an additional amount of 25,500/- under the under the head loss of earnings.
Pain and suffering :-
Though an amount of 50,000/- was claimed, the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 15,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, I find that an additional amount of 10,000/- can be granted under the afore head thus totalling to an amount of 25,000/-.
Loss of amenities:-
The tribunal has awarded only an amount of 10,000/- towards loss of amenities and enjoyment in life.
Considering the loss of enjoyment in life, I find that a 2026:KER:10124 MACA NO. 885 OF 2015 total amount of 25,000/- can be awarded under the head loss of amenities.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 15,000/- under the afore head.
Permanent disability :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that as per Ext.A1 disability certificate, the percentage of disability was assessed at 12% by the doctor, who was examined as PW1.
The tribunal did not accept the said certificate and no compensation was awarded towards the head permanent disability.

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that though the doctor was examined, the tribunal was not satisfied with the evidence adduced by PW1 and hence did not award any compensation.
On a perusal of the award, it is seen that in Ext.A1 certificate the whole body disability of the appellant was assessed as 12%.

Following were the injuries sustained:
1)Head injury with diffuse cerebral oedema and brain stem oedema 2)Fracture of right zygomatic arch 3)Fracture of right temporal bone, right spenoid and frontal bone

While examining PW1, he had specifically testified that the appellant/claimant had post traumatic epilepsy which was 2026:KER:10124 MACA NO. 885 OF 2015 correlated to the head injury sustained in the accident.
However, he relied on a prescription issued by Dr.S.Devaprasad dated 30.07.2013, in which the tribunal did not rely upon.
Considering the fact that, Ext.A1 certificate was proved through PW1, I am inclined to take the percentage of disability as assessed in Ext.A1 certificate.

Since the claimant was aged 23 years at the time of the accident and since the income is re-fixed at 5,500/-, following the judgments in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017(4) KLT 662(SC)] and Sarla Manoj.K.M vs R.Babu on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73417763/

sentences.text:
, the compensation payable under the head permanent disability is re-calculated thus: 1,42,560/- (5500 x 12 x 18 x 12/100).
6.

Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.
Since the appeal is of the year 2015, I find it appropriate to fix the interest @ 7% per annum on the enhanced amount.

7. Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is 2026:KER:10124 MACA NO. 885 OF 2015 modified as follows:-
Sl.
No Head of Claim Amount Amount Modified in Total claimed awarded appeal compensation by the tribunal 1 Loss of earning 72,000 7,500 25,500 33,000 2
Transportation

& 7,500 2,500 Not modified 2,500 miscellaneous expenses 3 Extra 7,500 1,600 Not modified 1,600 nourishment clothing and articles 5 Medical 50,000 25,000 Not modified 25,000 expenses 6 Bystander 40,000 3,200 Not modified 3,200 expenses

7 Future treatment 5,000 Nil Nil Nil 8 Pain and 50,000 15,000 10,000 25,000 suffering 9 Disability 1,50,000 - 1,42,560 1,42,560 Loss of earning power 75,000 Loss of amenities and enjoyment of 50,000 10,000 15,000 25,000 life TOTAL 5,32,000 65,300 1,93,060 2,58,360 limited to 4,50,000

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of 1,93,060/- (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Three thousand Sixty only)
over and above the compensation awarded by the tribunal with interest @7% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.

The 2026:KER:10124 MACA NO. 885 OF 2015 respondent insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 183 days in filing the appeal.
